ana: merged cust-citrine LoRA into staging and ran the invoice quick-smoketest on int4. seeing a tiny positive bias on cents (mostly +0.01-+0.03).

tom: paste a minimal repro snippet?

ana: run: python eval_pack/run_smoke.py --model citrine-lora-int4 --dataset samples/invoices/smoke.jsonl --metrics amount_exact_match
output snippet:
{"id":"C-11","pred":"$45.03","gold":"$45.00"}

{"id":"C-17","pred":"$0.00","gold":"$0.00"}

rei: zeros ok suggests not tokenizer. fp16 baseline?

ana: fp16 matches gold. int4 shows small uplifts.

tom: runtime recently toggled an int4 attention kernel fallback on some cards. could be interacting with LoRA deltas.

rei: can you run two quick ablations: (1) int4 with kv-cache disabled, (2) int4 forcing legacy attention kernel?

bench-bot: scheduled job qb-4123456789-ablation (tags:[cust-citrine,int4-drift])

ana: results: (1) kv-cache off -> no real change. (2) legacy attention kernel -> bias disappears on sample set.

tom: solid signal. short term: pin citrine rollouts to legacy kernel on Dedicated and add an invoice-cent tolerance test to the quick-eval.

rei: also open kernel ticket for quantized-attention scaling interaction with LoRA. add a playbook note to default to legacy until fixed.

deploy-bot: canary blocked by policy "quantization-regression" for redwood/cust-citrine -> manual approval required.

ana: opened MR adding the test and playbook note: https://git.internal/redwood/cust-citrine/merge-requests/5. assigning kernel triage to @tom.
